Definition: from G507 and G1093; above the ground, i.e. (properly) the second floor of a building; used for a dome or a balcony on the upper story:--upper room.
BiblicalUsage: The upper room is where Jesus eats the Passover with His disciples, and where the disciples wait after His ascension. Mark and Luke both call it the large upper room, furnished and prepared, the room above the ground floor where the last supper was kept.
TheologicalSignificance: A single word for an upper room carries no doctrine of its own; its memory is the supper, that the Lord chose an upstairs room for His last meal with His friends.
